official.description: Clark University's Global Scholars Program Scholarship is one of five merit scholarships for which international first-year students are eligible; consideration is based solely on the admission application without regard to financial need, and a separate essay is required. Clark states it is not able to offer financial assistance to cover the full cost of attendance, and its admissions process is need-aware, meaning an application may be denied on financial grounds if stated need exceeds what merit scholarships and need-based aid can meet.
official.program_type: Merit scholarship for international first-year undergraduate students
official.english_requirement: No specific minimum scores; general indicators: TOEFL iBT 85 overall with no sub-score below 20 (or 4.5 overall with no sub-score below 4 on the new scale from January 2026), IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-score below 6, Duolingo 120 overall with no sub-score below 100, or PTE 61 overall with no sub-score below 55. English proficiency is assessed holistically with scores, transcript, essay and recommendations.

verification.notes: Checked clarku.edu scholarships, international-student FAQ, financial-aid and international admissions pages on 2026-10-10: the Global Scholars Program Scholarship, its separate-essay requirement, deadlines and English rules are confirmed; no current official Clark page publishes a dollar amount for the award, so the amount is left null rather than carried over from third-party sites.

applicant_utility.summary: Clark's Global Scholars Program Scholarship is one of five first-year international merit awards, but unlike the automatic ones it requires its own separate essay on top of your admission application. Clark's current pages publish no dollar figure for the award, so treat the $15,000-per-year and $2,500-stipend numbers circulating on third-party sites as unverified until Clark's Office of Financial Assistance confirms them. Clark states outright that it cannot fund the full cost of attendance and that admissions are need-aware, so plan to show you can cover a large share of a roughly $82,000 total cost yourself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Well-rounded international first-year applicants with a strong global-leadership story who can fund a significant share of the cost and want merit consideration at a small research university.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply through the Common App or Coalition/Scoir by November 1 (Early Decision I / Early Action) or January 15 (Early Decision II / Regular Decision); there is no application fee.
Draft the separate Global Scholars essay early - it is the only way into this award and sits on top of the admission application.

Complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form on your Applicant Status Portal; it is the only accepted aid form (Clark does not take the ISFAA or CSS Profile).
Send transcripts covering your full last three years plus counselor and teacher recommendations; two years of records cannot be reviewed.
Book an accepted English test early: TOEFL iBT 85, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 120 or PTE 61 are Clark's general indicators.
common_rejection_risks: Skipping the separate Global Scholars essay - without it you are only in the running for the three automatic awards.
Underestimating need-aware admissions: the aid form's stated need can sink the admission itself if it exceeds what Clark can offer.
Assuming full funding; Clark says it cannot cover the full cost of attendance for international students.
Relying on recycled third-party figures for the award amount that Clark no longer publishes.
Submitting incomplete transcripts covering fewer than three years.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: 2026-27 billed charges total $77,970 (tuition $62,070, standard room, board and fees) and Clark's total estimated cost of attendance is about $82,753-$85,000 per year; the international admissions page states international students typically pay around $40,000 per year after scholarships and aid, so budget for the remainder plus travel and health insurance.
document_audit: All documents must be in English - include originals with certified translations where needed.
The Certification of Finances form only appears after you apply, on the Applicant Status Portal, so file it the moment it unlocks.
English scores: official agency reports are preferred, and a Duolingo score must be sent directly from the Duolingo portal.
Any private or external scholarship you win must be reported in writing to the Office of Financial Assistance.
alerts: Need-aware admissions: the financial picture you show on the Certification form can affect the admission decision, not just the aid offer.
Consideration is tied to the admission round - miss November 1 or January 15 and you miss the cycle.
Scholarship results arrive with the admission decision, so there is no later notification window to chase.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One admission application (Common App or Coalition/Scoir) plus the separate Global Scholars essay, with aid filed through the International Student Certification of Finances form on the status portal; scholarship outcomes come with the admission decision.

official.description: Michigan State University awards these merit scholarships to incoming first-year students with non-U.S. residency status; unless otherwise noted, the application for admission is all that is needed to be considered for each award. official.program_type: Admissions merit scholarships for non-resident international first-year students
official.english_requirement: TOEFL iBT 79 with no subscore below 17 for regular admission (new scale for tests on or after Jan. 21, 2026: score of 4 with no section below 4, except 3.5 for speaking); IELTS 6.5; Duolingo English Test 110; PTE Academic 53 (minimum subscore 48); MSUELT average 80. SAT/ACT are optional and not required for admission or scholarships. Three consecutive years of full-time U.S. high school from grade 9 with a 3.0+ GPA and no English language learning classes, or qualifying U.S. university study, can substitute.

applicant_utility.summary: MSU's international merit awards are automatic - there is no separate scholarship application, so your admission file is your scholarship application. The award is set by your academic record and how rigorous your curriculum was, tops out at $18,000 per year at the President's Award level, and renews for up to eight semesters if you hold 12 credits and good standing. Because the money is tuition-based only, living costs, housing, travel and fees stay on you, and only a limited number of considered students actually receive an offer.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong academic performers on challenging non-U.S. curricula who can self-fund living costs and want maximum scholarship consideration without a separate application.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the MSU admission application by Nov. 1 (early action) to lock in a decision by Jan. 15 and maximum scholarship consideration.
Self-report English scores if needed (TOEFL iBT 79+, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 110, PTE 53); official scores must follow from the testing agency before enrollment if admitted.
Make sure your transcript showcases curriculum rigor - award levels weigh the overall rigor and success within your curriculum, not just grades.
If a government or private sponsor pays your tuition, notify your admissions counselor early; sponsor support can adjust your award.
Pay the acceptance fee and confirm your enrollment for the semester the award is made - awards cannot be deferred.
common_rejection_risks: Treating automatic consideration as guaranteed - only a limited number of considered students get offers and meeting criteria guarantees nothing.
Changing residency status or accepting an international or out-of-state tuition waiver, which voids future renewals.
Dropping below 12 credit hours in any semester without prior written approval from the Office of Financial Aid.
Deferring the initial enrollment semester, which the award rules do not allow.
Counting on the Honors College money without an Honors College invitation - the $13,000 Excellence Scholarship and ~$3,500 Professorial Assistantship are invite-only.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, housing, meals, transportation, books and fees - these awards apply to tuition only, so even the top $18,000 President's Award covers just part of the non-resident bill.
document_audit: Official transcripts and certified exam results (IGCSE/GCSE/IB) must come directly from your school or testing agency; transcript notations alone do not count for English proof.
Self-reported test scores must be matched by official scores sent through the agency before you enroll (TOEFL 1465, SAT 1465, ACT 2032).
Provisional admittees must take the MSUELT on arrival, so keep the English file complete and unambiguous.
alerts: Residency trap: keeping the award through all eight semesters depends on maintaining international residency for tuition purposes.
The eight-semester cap includes semesters you were ineligible - an approved leave of absence still counts against the limit.
If enrollment is disrupted you must request an official leave of absence via es.scholarships@msu.edu or the award can stop.
Nov. 1 is the scholarship lever: it buys early action, maximum scholarship consideration and a decision guaranteed by Jan. 15.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single submission - the MSU admission application by Nov. 1 early action; awards are considered automatically, with decisions arriving by Jan. 15 (Non-resident Scholarship decisions by mid-February).
